Markdown draws a blank row where Rich's new_line puts one, not one per blank source line (rich-unfiled-791c.mk71)

Rich reads no blank line of the source: every element it exits sets
new_line (a rule and an image clear it), and a blank row goes ahead of
whatever it draws next while it is set. The renderer now walks the
document in Rich's order — images as met, top-level blocks as they exit —
and that flag is the only source of blank rows. Blank tokens and list
item gaps draw nothing; a rule draws its own blank row after it.

Also matches Rich for an empty quote (rich-unfiled-791c.erhp): no row,
and the row its exit puts ahead of the next block.

Markdown opens and closes fenced code as markdown-it's fence rule does, as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.fxsx) (#436)

* Markdown opens and closes fenced code as markdown-it's fence rule does, as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.fxsx)

A fence opens on three or more backticks whose info string holds no
backtick, or three or more tildes with any info string, and closes only on
a run of the same marker at least as long followed by spaces and tabs.
Checked token-for-token against markdown-it-py 4.2 over 3000 fuzzed
sources: 790 diffs before, 0 after.

* Markdown docs name tilde fences and the closing rule; the no-break-space test row is spelled as an escape (rich-unfiled-791c.fxsx)
